claim: A bucket policy can restrict access to a specific VPC endpoint with the aws:sourceVpce condition.
question: How do you limit an S3 bucket to one VPC endpoint?

evidence.quote: S3 bucket policies now support a condition, aws:sourceVpce, that you can use to restrict access.

claim: Amazon Macie uses machine learning to recognize sensitive data in S3, such as personally identifiable information (PII) or intellectual property, and shows where it is stored.
question: What does Amazon Macie find in S3?

evidence.quote: Amazon Macie uses machine learning to recognize sensitive data such as personally identifiable information (PII) or intellectual property, assigns a business value, and provides visibility into where this data is stored and how it is being used in your organization.

claim: IAM Access Analyzer for S3 alerts you when a bucket is configured to allow access to anyone on the internet or is shared with other AWS accounts.
question: What does IAM Access Analyzer for S3 report?

evidence.quote: Access Analyzer for S3 alerts you when you have a bucket that is configured to allow access to anyone on the internet or that is shared with other AWS accounts.

claim: You can configure a bucket to write access log records for all requests, or use AWS CloudTrail data events when you need IAM identity information in the logs.
question: How do you audit access to an S3 bucket?

evidence.quote: Yes, customers can optionally configure an Amazon S3 bucket to create access log records for all requests made against it. Alternatively, customers who need to capture IAM/user identity information in their logs can configure AWS CloudTrail Data Events.

claim: You cannot completely disable direct access through the bucket hostname, but a bucket policy can reject requests that are not made through an access point.
question: Can you force all access to go through S3 access points?

values.display: rejects requests not made using an access point

evidence.quote: Not currently, but you can attach a bucket policy that rejects requests not made using an access point.

claim: S3 is designed to provide 99.999999999% (11 nines) data durability.
question: What durability is S3 designed for?

evidence.quote: Based on its unique architecture, S3 is designed to provide 99.999999999% (11 nines) data durability.

claim: By default S3 stores data redundantly across a minimum of 3 Availability Zones.
question: Across how many Availability Zones does S3 store data by default?

values.spoken: a minimum of three Availability Zones

evidence.quote: Additionally, S3 stores data redundantly across a minimum of 3 Availability Zones (AZ) by default, providing built-in resilience against widespread disaster.

claim: S3 checks integrity end to end on every upload, confirms the data is stored redundantly before the upload succeeds, and keeps checking data at rest over time.
question: How does S3 achieve its durability in practice?

evidence.quote: S3 has end-to-end integrity checking on every object upload and verifies that all data is correctly and redundantly stored across multiple storage devices before it considers your upload to be successful. Once your data is stored in S3, S3 continuously monitors data durability over time with periodic integrity checks of all data at rest.

claim: If all or part of an Availability Zone is lost or damaged, data in a One Zone storage class may be lost.
question: Is One Zone data protected against the loss of its Availability Zone?

evidence.quote: In the unlikely case of the loss or damage to all or part of an AWS Availability Zone, data in a One Zone storage class may be lost.

claim: S3 One Zone-IA data is not resilient to the loss of availability or the physical loss of an Availability Zone; S3 Standard, S3 Intelligent-Tiering, S3 Standard-IA and the S3 Glacier classes are designed to withstand it.
question: Which storage classes survive the destruction of an Availability Zone?

values.display: not resilient to the loss of availability or physical loss of an Availability Zone

evidence.quote: However, data in the S3 One Zone-IA storage class is not resilient to the loss of availability or physical loss of an Availability Zone. In contrast, S3 Standard, S3 Intelligent-Tiering, S3 Standard-Infrequent Access, and the S3 Glacier storage classes are designed to withstand loss of availability or the destruction of an Availability Zone.

claim: S3 durability does not protect against accidental or malicious deletes; you still need to decide what to keep and which controls protect against wrong deletes.
question: Does S3 durability mean you do not need backups?

values.display: does not protect against accidental or malicious deletes

evidence.quote: Yes. Amazon S3’s durability system does not protect against accidental or malicious deletes. S3 relies on customers to decide what data they want to keep, what data they want to get rid of, and what optional controls they need to protect against deletes that are incorrect, either due to accidents or malice.

claim: When you tell S3 to delete data, it is deleted immediately and cannot be recovered by AWS.
question: Can AWS recover an object you deleted from S3?

evidence.quote: When you tell Amazon S3 to delete data, that data is immediately deleted, and it cannot be recovered by AWS.

claim: S3 Versioning, S3 Replication and S3 Object Lock are optional features that add protection beyond durability; a backup application can also back up bucket data.
question: Which S3 features protect against accidental or malicious deletes?

values.display: S3 Object Versioning, S3 Replication, and S3 Object Lock

evidence.quote: S3 Object Versioning, S3 Replication, and S3 Object Lock are all optional features that you can use to add additional data protection, beyond the durability that S3 automatically provides. In addition, you can use a backup application to back up all or part of the data in your S3 buckets.

claim: For upload and download integrity checks you can choose SHA-1, SHA-512, SHA-256, CRC32, CRC32C, CRC64NVME, MD5, XXHash64, XXHash3 or XXHash128.
question: Which checksum algorithms can you choose for S3 uploads and downloads?

evidence.quote: You can choose a SHA-1, SHA-512, SHA-256, CRC32, CRC32C, CRC64NVME, MD5, XXHash64, XXHash3, or XXHash128 checksum algorithm, depending on your application needs.

claim: The latest AWS SDKs automatically calculate CRC-based checksums for all uploads, and S3 independently verifies the checksum before accepting the object.
question: Do AWS SDKs compute checksums for S3 uploads by default?

evidence.quote: In addition, the latest AWS SDKs automatically calculate efficient CRC-based checksums for all uploads. S3 independently verifies that checksum and only accepts objects after confirming that data integrity was maintained in transit over the public internet.

claim: If the SDK does not pre-calculate a checksum, S3 calculates a CRC-based checksum of the whole object, even for multipart uploads.
question: What does S3 do when the client sends no checksum?

values.display: whole object, even for multipart uploads

evidence.quote: If a version of the SDK that does not provide pre-calculated checksums is used to upload an object, S3 calculates a CRC-based checksum of the whole object, even for multipart uploads.

claim: Once Versioning is enabled, S3 preserves existing objects on every PUT, POST, COPY or DELETE; by default a GET returns the most recently written version.
question: What does S3 Versioning do on overwrite and delete, and which version does GET return?

evidence.quote: Once you enable Versioning for a bucket, Amazon S3 preserves existing objects anytime you perform a PUT, POST, COPY, or DELETE operation on them. By default, GET requests will retrieve the most recently written version.

claim: After a DELETE, simple (un-versioned) requests no longer retrieve the object, but all versions remain and can be restored; only the bucket owner can permanently delete a version.
question: After a delete in a versioned bucket, who can permanently remove a version?

values.display: Only the owner of an Amazon S3 bucket can permanently delete a version

evidence.quote: When a user performs a DELETE operation on an object, subsequent simple (un-versioned) requests will no longer retrieve the object. However, all versions of that object will continue to be preserved in your Amazon S3 bucket and can be retrieved or restored. Only the owner of an Amazon S3 bucket can permanently delete a version.

claim: With Versioning and MFA Delete, permanently deleting a version needs two forms of authentication: your AWS account credentials and a valid six-digit code from a physical authentication device.
question: What does MFA Delete require to permanently delete an object version?

evidence.quote: If you enable Versioning with MFA Delete on your Amazon S3 bucket, two forms of authentication are required to permanently delete a version of an object: your AWS account credentials and a valid six-digit code and serial number from an authentication device in your physical possession.

claim: Lifecycle rules plus Versioning can give a rollback window, for example by archiving previous versions to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and deleting them after 100 days.
question: How do you build a recycle-bin style rollback window on S3?

evidence.quote: For example, with your versioning-enabled bucket, you can set up a rule that archives all of your previous versions to the lower-cost S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class and deletes them after 100 days, giving you a 100-day window to roll back any changes on your data while lowering your storage costs.

claim: S3 Object Lock prevents an object version from being deleted or overwritten for a period you define or indefinitely, to enforce retention or meet regulatory compliance.
question: What does S3 Object Lock do?

evidence.quote: Amazon S3 Object Lock is an Amazon S3 feature that prevents an object version from being deleted or overwritten for a period of time that you define or indefinitely, so that you can enforce retention policies as an added layer of data protection or for regulatory compliance.

claim: Object Lock protection stays in place regardless of the storage class and through Lifecycle transitions between classes.
question: Does a Lifecycle transition remove Object Lock protection?

evidence.quote: S3 Object Lock protection is maintained regardless of which storage class the object version resides in and throughout S3 Lifecycle transitions between storage classes.

claim: In Governance Mode, accounts with specific IAM permissions can remove WORM protection; in Compliance Mode, no user can remove it, including the root account.
question: What is the difference between Object Lock governance mode and compliance mode?

evidence.quote: When deployed in Governance Mode, AWS accounts with specific IAM permissions are able to remove WORM protection from an object version. If you require stronger immutability in order to comply with regulations, you can use Compliance Mode. In Compliance Mode, WORM protection cannot be removed by any user, including the root account.

claim: A Legal Hold keeps an object version from being modified or deleted indefinitely until it is explicitly removed.
question: How long does an Object Lock legal hold last?

evidence.quote: A Legal Hold prevents an object version from being modified or deleted indefinitely until it is explicitly removed.

claim: Object Lock has two retention types: fixed, where you set the Retain Until Date, and variable, where you turn on an event hold and S3 sets the Retain Until Date when you release the hold.
question: What are the fixed and variable retention types in Object Lock?

evidence.quote: With fixed retention, you specify the Retain Until Date when you apply the retention period. With variable retention, you defer the Retain Until Date — you turn on an event hold, and Amazon S3 sets the Retain Until Date when you release the hold.
